Rashi on Ketubot 48b:10:1.english: In what [case] are these words said - That delivering her to the agents constitutes marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:10:2.english: To inherit [from] her - For this matter alone is it [considered] marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:10:3.english: A refutation of all of them - Those who disagree with Shmuel.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:11:1.hebrew: הא סתמא - אם נכנסה ושהתה עמו סתם, אמרינן נשואין נינהו, וזו היא כניסת חופתה, ואע"פ שלא נבעלה הוי נשואין:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:11:1.english: [But if she entered] without specification - If she entered and stayed with him without specification, we say it is marriage, and this is her entry into the bridal canopy, and even though she has not had intercourse, it is [considered] marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:12:1.hebrew: סתמי סתמי קתני - הא דקתני נכנסה עמו ללון, לא שפירשה "ללון אני נכנסת ולא לשם נשואין"; והא דקתני נכנסה עמו לנשואין, לא שפירשה "לנשואין אני נכנסת", אלא זו וזו שנכנסה סתם. ותנא הוא דקאמר, דהיכא דחצר שלה — סתם כניסתה לא לנשואין הן אלא ללון, והיכא דחצר שלו — סתם כניסתה לשם נשואין:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:12:1.english: [The tanna] teaches [two] unspecified [cases] - That which [the baraita] teaches, "she entered with him to lodge," [means] not that she explicitly stated, "I am entering to lodge and not for the sake of marriage"; and that which it teaches, "she entered with him for marriage," [means] not that she explicitly stated, "I am entering for marriage." Rather, both this [case] and that [case refer to] when she entered without specification. And it is the tanna who is stating that where the courtyard is hers, her unspecified entry is not for marriage, but rather to lodge; and where the courtyard is his, her unspecified entry is for the sake of marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:13:1.english: She is [sentenced] to strangulation - like a married woman, and not to stoning like a betrothed woman.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:14:1.hebrew: ואימא פרט לכשנכנסה לחופה ולא נבעלה - דייך אם מיעטת כגון זו, דלא תימא נערה בתולה כתיב גבי סקילה, והא אכתי בתולה הואי. אבל זו שאף לחופה לא נכנסה לא מיעטה הכתוב, ואכתי בית אביה קרינא ביה:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:14:1.english: And say [that it is] excluding [the case of] when she entered the wedding canopy and had not [yet] had intercourse - It suffices for you if you excluded [a case] like this, so that you should not say: "A virgin maiden" is written regarding stoning, and this [woman] is still a virgin. However, this [woman] who has not even entered the wedding canopy, Scripture did not exclude, and we still call it "her father's house."

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:15:1.hebrew: חופה - בלא בעילה, בהדיא כתיבא דלאו בסקילה היא. וכי איצטריך האי, למסירה:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:15:1.english: Wedding canopy - Without intercourse, it is explicitly written that she is not [subject] to stoning. And when this [verse] is needed, [it is] for handing over.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:16:1.english: If we say [that she is] actually married - [Meaning] that she entered the wedding canopy and had intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:1:1.hebrew: לרשות הבעל לנשואין - כלומר, שתכנס לחופה לשם נשואין, שתהא מסורה לרשות הבעל:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:1:1.english: To the husband's authority for marriage - That is to say, that she enters the wedding canopy for the sake of marriage, so that she is handed over to the husband's authority.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:1:2.hebrew: מסרו שלוחי האב - שהיה האב משלחה לו ע"י שלוחיו, ופגעו בשלוחי הבעל ומסרוה להם:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:1:2.english: The father's messengers delivered - For the father was sending her to him through his messengers, and they met the husband's messengers and delivered her to them.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:2:1.hebrew: ממשנה ראשונה - בפרק אע"פ:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:2:1.english: From the initial Mishnah - In the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:2:2.hebrew: הגיע זמן - שנים עשר חדש לבתולה משתבעה הבעל להכין עצמה לנשואין, ולאלמנה שלשים יום:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:2:2.english: The time arrived - Twelve months for a virgin from when the husband claimed her, to prepare herself for marriage, and for a widow, thirty days.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:2:3.english: And they were not married - For example, where the groom delayed, or [due to] an unavoidable circumstance on his part.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:2:4.english: And they eat teruma - If she is an Israelite woman betrothed to a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:3:1.hebrew: מסירתה לכל - ליורשה, וליטמא לה, ולמעשה ידיה, ולכל דבר איש באשה, קיימא מסירת שלוחים במקום חופה:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:3:1.english: Her delivery [is] for all [respects] - To inherit from her, and to become ritually impure for her, and for her handiwork, and for every matter of a husband with a wife, delivery [to the husband's] agents stands in place of chuppah.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:3:2.hebrew: חוץ מאכילת תרומה - דטעמא דידה משום סימפון, כדלקמן בפרק אע"פ (כתובות דף נז:), ואכתי איכא למיחש להכי, שמא ימצאו בה מומין ויהיו קידושיה ונישואיה טעות:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:3:2.english: Except for eating terumah - For the reason for it is because of simpon [potential voiding of the marriage due to hidden defects], as [explained] later in the chapter Af Al Pi (Ketubot 57b), and there is still [reason] to be concerned about this, lest blemishes be found in her and her betrothal and marriage be in error.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:3:3.hebrew: ורב אסי אמר אף לתרומה - קסבר, הא דאמור רבנן ארוסה לא תאכל בתרומה, משום שמא ימזגו לה כוס בבית אביה ותשקה לאחיה ולאחיותיה [שם]. והשתא דאין אחיה ואחיותיה אצלה, שרי:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:3:3.english: And Rav Asi said: Even with regard to terumah - He holds [that] that which the Sages said, [that] a betrothed woman may not partake of terumah, [is] because perhaps they will mix a cup [of wine] for her in her father's house and she will give [it] to her brothers and sisters [there] to drink. Now that her brothers and sisters are not with her, it is permitted.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:4:1.hebrew: לעולם היא ברשות האב - ואוקימנא דהאי לעולם משום אכילת תרומה נקט לה, וקתני עד שתכנס לחופה:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:4:1.english: She is always under [her] father’s authority - And we established that this [word] "always" was stated with regard to eating terumah, and [yet] it teaches: "until she enters the wedding canopy."

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:4:2.english: Rav said to them - To his student and his son.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:4:3.hebrew: לא תיזלו בתר איפכא - לא תשיבו בבית המדרש ממשנה הנהפכת לשני צדדים, שיוכל המתרץ לתרץ משמעה אחר דבריו:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:4:3.english: Do not go after that which can be inverted - Do not raise an objection in the study hall from a Mishnah that can be turned two ways, such that the respondent can interpret its meaning [to accord] with his words.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:5:1.hebrew: שמואל אמר לירושתה - הוא דמהניא מסירה, שאם מתה בדרך, בעל יורש נדונייתה; דאע"ג דאמר מר (לקמן כתובות דף נג.) אשתו ארוסה מתה אינו יורשה, הכא, כיון דמסרה, אחולי אחיל אב מהשתא מחמת קירוב נישואין. אבל לתרומה, ולהפרת נדריה שלא בשותפות, ולמציאתה — דאינה אלא משום איבה, ואכתי ליכא למיחש להכי — לא מהניא מסירה כי חופה:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:5:1.english: Shmuel said: To her inheritance - [It is only for this] that delivery is effective, that if she dies on the way, [her] husband inherits her dowry; for even though the master said (below, Ketubot 53a): "[If] his betrothed wife dies, he does not inherit her," here, since [her father] has delivered her, the father waives [his rights] from now on because of the imminence of the marriage. However, for terumah, and for the annulment of her vows without partnership [with the father], and for her found objects — which is only because of [avoiding] enmity, and there is not yet [any need] to be concerned about this — delivery is not effective like the wedding canopy.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:6:1.hebrew: לכתובתה - הוא דמהניא מסירה, והשתא קא בעי הש"ס למילתיה:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:6:1.english: To her marriage contract - [that] is what [the] delivery is effective for, and now the Talmud asks about his statement.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:6:2.english: What is it? That if she dies, he inherits - [That is,] the husband [inherits] the dowry that the father pledged to her.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:6:3.hebrew: לומר כתובתה מאחר מנה - לשוייה אלמנה מן הנשואין, שלא תיקנו לה חכמים אלא מנה מן הכונסה אחרי כן:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:6:3.english: To say [that] her marriage contract from another [is] one hundred [dinars] - To render her a widow from marriage, for the Sages instituted for her only one hundred [dinars] from the one who marries her afterward.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:8:1.english: The father went, etc. - His handing [her] over is not a [valid] handing over.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:8:2.hebrew: ונכנסה עמו - עם בעלה ללון, כשאר לינה בדרך בעלמא, ולא לשם נשואין:
Rashi on Ketubot 48b:8:2.english: And she entered with him - With her husband to lodge, like an ordinary lodging on the way, and not for the sake of marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 48b:8:3.english: That her marriage contract - [This refers to] movable property that her father designated for her dowry.

Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:10:1.hebrew: תיובתא דכולהו - לאו דווקא דכולהו, אלא להנהו דאמרי "אף לתרומה". וכענין זה מצינו ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכט:) גבי מחלק נכסיו על פיו: "תיובתא דכולהו", אע"ג דלא הוי תיובתא אלא לחד:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:10:1.english: A refutation of all of them - Not literally "of all of them," rather [it refers] to those who say "also for terumah." And similarly we find in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 129b) regarding one who distributes his property orally: "a refutation of all of them," even though it is a refutation of only one [opinion].

Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:16:1.hebrew: היינו בתולה ולא בעולה - וא"ת: אימא "ולא נשואה" שנכנסה לחופה ונבעלה שלא כדרכה, דאכתי בתולה היא, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף ט:): "באו עליה עשרה ועדיין היא בתולה — כולן בסקילה"! ויש לומר, דהא אמר התם דבעל עושה אותה בעולה שלא כדרכה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:16:1.english: This [is the same as] "a virgin and not a non-virgin" - And if you say: say [that "a married woman" refers to one] who entered the wedding canopy and had intercourse in an unnatural manner, for she is still a virgin, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (9b): "If ten men had intercourse with her and she is still a virgin, all of them are [liable] to stoning"! And one can say [in answer] that it states there that a husband renders her a non-virgin [even] through unnatural intercourse.

Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:2:1.hebrew: לאפוקי ממשנה ראשונה - אע"ג דתנן בהדיא בפ' אע"פ (לקמן כתובות דף נז.): "זו משנה ראשונה, ב"ד של אחריהם אמרו כו'", כן דרך התנאים להשמיענו בקוצר אע"ג דכבר השמיענו במקום אחר; וכה"ג איכא בריש ברכות (דף ב:):
Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:2:1.english: To exclude the initial Mishnah - Even though we learned explicitly in the chapter [entitled] Af al Pi (later, Ketubot 57a): "This is the initial Mishnah; the court after them said, etc.", such is the way of the Tannaim, to teach us briefly even though they already taught us [it] in another place; and similarly there is [such a case] at the beginning of Berakhot (2b).

Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:3:1.hebrew: רב אסי אמר אף לתרומה - פי' בקונטרס: דקסבר רב אסי דטעמא דאין ארוסה בת ישראל אוכלת בתרומה כדעולא — "שמא ימזגו לה כוס", וכיון שמסרה, תו ליכא למיחש. וקשה לר"י: דאפי' עולא, דמפרש טעמא דמשנה ראשונה "שמא ימזגו לה כוס", למשנה אחרונה מודה דטעמא משום סימפון; וע"כ רב אסי איירי לפי משנה אחרונה, דאמתני' קאי, ומפקה מתני' ממשנה ראשונה מדקתני "לעולם", ועוד דאיתותב מברייתא דלקמן, ולא משני ההיא כמשנה אחרונה. ונראה לר"י דטעמא דרב אסי משום סימפון, ומשמסרה תו ליכא למיחש, דמסתמא בדקי לה. וקשה: דרב אסי חייש לסימפון בהגעת זמן טפי מבמסר האב לשלוחי הבעל, ובפ' אע"פ (לקמן כתובות דף נח.) אמרי' איפכא! דקאמר: מאי בינייהו בין למאן דאמר משום סימפון בין למ"ד משום "שמא תשקה"? איכא בינייהו "קיבל מסר והלך" — פירוש: מסר האב לשלוחי הבעל — דלמאן דאמר משום סימפון איכא, אע"ג דבהגיע זמן לא חיישינן לסימפון למשנה ראשונה. ואור"י דודאי סברא הוא דבמשנה אחרונה, דחיישינן לסימפון בהגעת זמן, כל שכן במסר, כדאמרינן התם; אבל הכא, רב אסי מתניתין דחקתיה, דקתני "הרי היא ברשות הבעל", דמשמע לגמרי — אפילו לתרומה. ועוד אור"י דמצינו לפרש ד"איכא בינייהו" — למאן דאמר סימפון ליכא, דבמסר לא חיישינן לסימפון, ולמאן דאמר "שמא ימזגו" איכא, דחיישינן שמא תשקה לשלוחי הבעל; ובקונטרס לא פירש התם כן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:3:1.english: Rav Asi said: Even [with regard] to terumah - Rashi explained that Rav Asi holds that the reason a betrothed Israelite woman [betrothed to a priest] does not eat terumah is in accordance with Ulla — [namely,] "lest they mix a cup [of terumah wine] for her" [in her father's house] — and once [her father] has delivered her [to the husband's messengers], there is no longer [reason] to be concerned. And this is difficult for R"I: for even Ulla, who explains the reason of the earlier Mishnah [as] "lest they mix a cup for her," agrees regarding the later Mishnah that the reason is because of simpon [annulment due to hidden bodily defects]; and perforce Rav Asi is speaking according to the later Mishnah, since he is addressing our Mishnah, and our Mishnah is excluded from the earlier Mishnah based on what it teaches: "forever" [le'olam], and furthermore, because [Rav Asi] is refuted from the baraita below, and [the Gemara] does not answer [that] that [baraita] is according to the later Mishnah. Rather, it appears to R"I that Rav Asi's reason is because of simpon, and once he has delivered her, there is no longer [reason] to be concerned, because presumably they [the husband's side] have [already] examined her. Yet this is difficult: for [according to this], Rav Asi is more concerned about simpon when the appointed time [for marriage] arrives than when the father delivers [her] to the husband's messengers, whereas in Chapter Af Al Pi (below, Ketubot 58a), we say the opposite! For [the Gemara] says: What is the practical difference between the one who says [the reason is] because of simpon and the one who says [it is] because of "lest she give [others] to drink"? There is a difference between them [in the case of] "he received, delivered, and went" — meaning, the father delivered [her] to the husband's messengers — for according to the one who says [it is] because of simpon, there is [still a concern], even though when the appointed time arrives we are not concerned for simpon according to the earlier Mishnah. And R"I says that certainly it is logical that in the later Mishnah, where we are concerned for simpon when the appointed time arrives, all the more so [are we concerned] when he has delivered [her], as we say there; however, here our Mishnah forced Rav Asi [to say this], because it teaches "behold she is under the husband's authority," which implies completely — even for terumah. And furthermore, R"I says that we can explain [the passage there] that "there is a difference between them" [means]: according to the one who says simpon, there is no [concern], because when he has delivered [her] we are not concerned for simpon, whereas according to the one who says "lest they mix [a cup]," there is [a concern], because we are concerned lest she give [terumah wine] to the husband's messengers to drink; and Rashi did not explain it that way there.

Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:5:1.hebrew: ושמואל אמר לירושתה - לא אתא לאפוקי הפרת נדרים, דהא תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל בסמוך דהויא ברשות הבעל להפרת נדריה, ויצתה מרשות האב. ונראה דהוא הדין מיטמא לה, כיון דאפקה רחמנא מסקילה לחנק, דמהתם יליף לכל מילי. אלא למעוטי תרומה אתי, וירושתה נקט לרבותא: דלא מיבעיא ליטמא לה ולהפרת נדריה דהויא מסירה כחופה, אלא אפילו ליורשה — דהוה ס"ד, כיון דירושת הבעל תקנתא דרבנן היא, הכא במסר לא תקון; אי נמי ס"ד דאין האב מזכה לבתו עד שתכנס לחופה — אפ"ה יורשה. אי נמי: אף כתובה דריש לקיש אתא למעוטי, וריש לקיש נמי "לא מיבעיא" קאמר, ולא אתא למעוטי אלא תרומה. אי נמי: ממעט נמי ירושתה מטעמא דפרישית:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48b:5:1.english: And Shmuel said: [With regard] to her inheritance - [Shmuel] does not come to exclude the annulment of vows, for the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael teaches shortly [below] that she is under the husband's authority with regard to the annulment of her vows, and she has left the father's authority. And it appears that the same applies to [her husband] contracting ritual impurity for her [to bury her], since the Merciful One removed her from [the penalty of] stoning to strangulation, for from there [the Tanna] derives [her status] for all matters. Rather, he comes to exclude teruma, and he mentioned "her inheritance" to teach a greater novelty: that it is unnecessary [to state] that with regard to contracting ritual impurity for her and the annulment of her vows, delivery [to the husband's messengers] is like [entering] the wedding canopy, but even with regard to inheriting her — where it might have entered your mind [to say] that since a husband's inheritance is a rabbinic enactment, here, where [the father] delivered [her], they did not enact [it]; alternatively, it might have entered your mind [to say] that a father does not transfer [rights to] his daughter until she enters the wedding canopy — even so, he inherits her. Alternatively: [Shmuel] also comes to exclude the ketubah [ruling] of Reish Lakish, and Reish Lakish likewise speaks in the style of "it is unnecessary [to say]," and only comes to exclude teruma. Alternatively: [Reish Lakish] also excludes her inheritance, for the reason that I explained:
